actions.justification: Mandatory first step: assess hemodynamic stability to determine urgency of transfusion and guide further management.
Mandatory: determine if active bleeding is present, which drives transfusion thresholds and potential need for massive transfusion protocol.
Mandatory: review prior transfusion history to identify alloantibodies, prior reactions, and transfusion requirements.
Mandatory action: CBC is required to determine hemoglobin level and guide transfusion decisions per guideline.
Mandatory action: Type and screen is required to prepare for potential blood product administration and ensure compatibility.

Optional but clinically indicated: Assessing symptoms of anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, chest pain, dizziness) will help determine whether a liberal or restrictive transfusion threshold is appropriate for this patient.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%) with normal vitals. Evidence-based guidelines support a restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7-8 g/dL) for stable patients, which reduces unnecessary transfusion risks such as TACO, TRALI, and transfusion reactions while maintaining equivalent outcomes compared to liberal strategies.
Pre-medication with acetaminophen is recommended prior to blood transfusion to reduce febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions, which is standard practice in transfusion protocols.
Pre-medication with diphenhydramine (antihistamine) is recommended prior to transfusion to reduce the risk of allergic transfusion reactions, particularly in patients with a transfusion history.
Ensuring reliable IV access is essential for ongoing transfusion support and medication delivery in this patient being managed for anemia/transfusion needs.
Maintaining normothermia is critical during transfusion management to prevent hypothermia-induced coagulopathy and cardiac complications.
Calcium gluconate supplementation is indicated to counteract hypocalcemia from citrate chelation in patients receiving blood products, supporting cardiac function and coagulation.
Patient is awaiting CBC results; serial vital sign monitoring every 15 minutes ensures early detection of hemodynamic changes or transfusion reactions while workup is pending.
Coagulation status should be assessed to guide potential transfusion decisions, especially if active bleeding or coagulopathy is suspected alongside the pending CBC.
Iron studies help differentiate causes of anemia (iron deficiency vs. other etiologies), guiding appropriate treatment decisions once CBC results return.
Direct antiglobulin test (DAT) is indicated to evaluate for hemolytic transfusion reaction or autoimmune hemolytic anemia, which is relevant given the transfusion workup context and pending CBC.
Reticulocyte count helps assess bone marrow response to anemia and distinguish between hypoproliferative and hemolytic/blood loss etiologies, complementing the iron studies already ordered.

Thromboelastography (TEG) provides real-time assessment of coagulation status and guides targeted blood product administration if needed, especially relevant given coagulation monitoring is already in progress.
Patient is at 90 minutes with CBC pending. Serial hemodynamic reassessment is critical to detect any deterioration in status while awaiting lab results, given the transfusion/bleeding context.
Blood bank workup (type and crossmatch confirmation, antibody screen results) is needed to prepare compatible blood products if transfusion becomes necessary once CBC results return.

With CBC pending and a transfusion-related workup in progress, reassessing hemoglobin level is essential to determine transfusion threshold decisions (restrictive vs liberal) once results are available.

With CBC pending and prior restrictive threshold applied, transfuse pRBC if hemoglobin falls below 7 g/dL per standard restrictive transfusion guidelines for stable patients without active cardiac disease.
If there is any concern for active or occult bleeding contributing to anemia, tranexamic acid can reduce fibrinolysis and blood loss, supporting hemostatic management while labs are pending.

Patient has undergone extensive workup and reassessment. Apply liberal transfusion threshold (Hb <8) given clinical context and completed monitoring, to ensure adequate oxygen delivery while awaiting final CBC results.
